affiliations.occupation: Waiter or waitress, except private family
affiliations.date_precision: The official Army-entry record carries civilian occupation code 227 on August 4, 1943; no employer, establishment, or exact job title is named.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact private identifier confirms identity. The code groups waiter and waitress work and identifies no employer, establishment, location, or Army-to-OSS sequence.

affiliations.date_precision: A 1945-1946 Boston University alumni notice says Bernique would resume his New Bedford law practice while on terminal leave; it does not give the practice's original dates or prove it immediately preceded military service.
affiliations.research_notes: The source's verb 'resume,' combined with its military and OSS chronology, supports an earlier private law practice. It does not establish the exact end date, a named firm, or that the practice was the immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer.

affiliations.date_precision: Documented in the September 1934 alumni periodical; exact start and end dates are unstated.
affiliations.research_notes: The 1934 source explicitly names the employer, title, city, class year, and unusual full name. A 1952 notice independently repeats the same name and class year and identifies his wartime colonel rank. The eight-year gap prevents labeling this the immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed First Lieutenant Roger P. Bernique is the Boston University law alumnus later identified as an OSS intelligence-mission chief in Indochina.
claims.evidence_excerpt: chief of the intelligence mission of the O.S.S. in Indo-China
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary Boston University notice gives the rare exact full name, Captain rank, Military Intelligence School chronology, and OSS Indochina assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare exact name, matching middle initial, compatible progression from first lieutenant to captain, and explicit OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The notice places Military Intelligence School completion in December 1942 and the OSS Indochina mission soon afterward.
claims.match_notes: The index's private officer identifier is not exposed. No employer is inferred from his later Justice Department work.

claims.claim_text: Roger P. Bernique had an individual law practice in New Bedford before the end of his wartime service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: While Bernique was on terminal leave, Bostonia reported that he would resume his law practice in the Merchants National Bank Building in New Bedford.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the rare exact name, compatible rank, Boston University law-class context, and explicit OSS chronology in the same notice.
claims.temporal_assessment: The verb 'resume' establishes an earlier practice, but the notice does not prove its exact dates or that it immediately preceded military or OSS service.
claims.match_notes: No law firm is named, so the practice is modeled as self-employment. It is not marked immediate pre-OSS or last civilian employer.

claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact name and colonel rank align with a contemporary alumni obituary, while a research essay supplies a precise NARA locator for Berno's OSS/SEAC report.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the rare exact full name, matching colonel rank, repeated Ohio Wesleyan class of 1927, wartime government service, and named OSS/SEAC archival report.
claims.temporal_assessment: The archival citation dates Berno's OSS/SEAC report to January 1945; the underlying document still requires direct review.

claims.claim_text: Philip B. Berns's printed private identifier conflicts with the official Army merged file, where the same identifier belongs to Donald J. Kreusch rather than Philip B. Berns.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The identifier printed beside Philip B. Berns in the OSS index resolves to a different full name in the official Army-entry file; the identifier itself is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Conflicting: the index row is visually clear, but its private identifier does not corroborate the indexed name in the official Army file.
claims.temporal_assessment: The incompatible Army record dates to 1940 and cannot be attached to Philip B. Berns's biography or employment history.
claims.match_notes: No Army occupation, birth-year code, or entry chronology from the incompatible record is assigned to Philip B. Berns. Box 52 must resolve whether the index contains a transcription error or represents another record problem.
